events.label: Reddit (RDDT) joins S&P 500 — passive demand concentrated at Aug 17 closing auction
events.note: Updated Aug 14 night: RDDT closed $178.09 (+12.7% from ~$157 Thursday close) — at the high end of the pre-inclusion window. Passive funds tracking the S&P 500 must hold RDDT before the Aug 18 open; the Aug 17 closing auction concentrates the mechanical peak buying. Post-mechanics test: RDDT holding above $177 for two sessions after Aug 18 = fundamental demand (advertising durability in AI-search environment) supports the passive bid. Reversion below $158 (pre-announcement close) within two sessions = purely mechanical pop. SPCX Nasdaq-100 inclusion precedent (July): mechanical gains can unwind substantially without fundamental support.

events.label: SPCX next staggered tranche (~7%) — second unlock after Aug 6 first tranche
events.note: Updated Aug 14 morning: SPCX $142.31 (Aug 13 close); August 20 is 6 days away. Macro has improved materially: September hike odds ~33%, CPI core 2.5%, PPI 0.0%. Oil triggers remain active: WTI $81.27 (above $79), Brent $87.18 (above $85). Rate relief has been absorbed above $128. Front-run signal: close below $120 on elevated volume before Aug 20. Morgan Stanley $140, Bernstein $248, Citi $200 targets. October Q3 earnings (Starlink profitability) is the narrative anchor. The Aug 14 30Y drift to ~5.19% is a modestly constructive development for the rate-compression side of the absorption thesis, but oil trigger clearance remains the blocking condition.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — three altitude ceiling sector confirmations raise the bar
events.note: Updated Aug 14 night: NVDA closed ~$225.38 (+0.04%), second consecutive close above $225 resistance. The altitude ceiling now spans three AI infrastructure sectors: CSCO (networking, −8.5% cumulative on a beat-and-raise), AMAT (semiconductor equipment, −3.89% AH on EPS beat and strong guide), and AVGO (networking silicon, −4.1% on VMware exploitation + 72% AI revenue concentration). All three delivered results at or near estimates and declined. The bar for August 26: gross margin above 78% AND data-center guide materially above the most aggressive sell-side estimate — both conditions must hold simultaneously. Meeting either alone fits the pattern established by the three prior prints. September hike odds ~31%, 30Y ~5.22% (auction stop-through). Jackson Hole (Aug 27) begins the day after the print — no de-risk window between NVDA's result and macro volatility.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote; September odds at 31%
events.note: Updated Aug 14 night: September hike odds ~31% after five consecutive soft data prints (NFP −23K, CPI core 2.5%, PPI flat, retail sales −0.6% MoM, UMich prelim 51.0 vs 54.5). 30Y at ~5.22% (auction stop-through from 5.24% secondary) — 7bps above the 5.15% de-escalation target. Warsh has described his keynote as a 'blank piece of paper' — no pre-commitment. Key new variable: UMich final reading is due Aug 28 (during Jackson Hole), within the symposium window. If the final confirms 51.0 with elevated inflation expectations, Warsh is speaking alongside real-time evidence of deteriorating consumer confidence. A data-dependent patience message compresses 30Y toward 5.10% and September odds below 25%. A supply-inflation hawkish message (SPR at 40-year lows, Hormuz disruption, UMich inflation expectations) re-anchors 30Y above 5.28%. NVDA earnings land Aug 26 — one day before the keynote, no de-risk window.

events.label: AVGO Q3 FY2026 earnings (est.) — VMware liability and AI concentration: first post-exploitation read
events.note: Added Aug 14 night: AVGO fell 4.1% to $389.79 on August 14 on two simultaneous headwinds: VMware CVE-2026-59310 active exploitation (361 IPs, 47 countries) and guidance implying AI accounts for ~72% of next-quarter sequential revenue growth. Q3 FY2026 results (est. early September, approximately September 4-5 based on Q2 reporting June 3) are the first public accounting of both: whether VMware remediation costs appear in the financial guidance, whether enterprise customers cited the incident, and whether AI revenue breadth (or concentration) shifts the multiple conversation. At ~65x trailing P/E, any miss or margin compression compounds. The $380 structural support level and $400 resistance are the two levels to monitor heading into the print.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
